task: My niece Priya turns 9 this Sunday and she's obsessed with horses and the Harry Potter books. Write a short birthday card message from her Auntie Jo that I can write inside a card with a horse on the front.
rewrite:
ambition:     A top card-writer would make it sound like Auntie Jo talking to this one child, with one playful joke that mixes her two loves (a Hogwarts-letter-style "we are pleased to inform you" for turning 9, or a Hippogriff/Buckbeak nod) instead of generic "Happy Birthday, hope it's magical."
agency:       The raw material is Priya's own favorites: which book, character, or horse she talks about most, plus a real shared memory with Auntie Jo. That isn't in reach, so assume the broad themes (horses, Harry Potter, turning 9) and leave out any invented specific.
acceleration: Use the Hogwarts acceptance-letter format ("Dear Priya, we are pleased to inform you...") or a Hippogriff/Thestral reference as the hook, and a short warm closing line. Keep it to 3-4 handwritable lines, pitched at a 9-year-old reader.
accuracy:     Nothing outside the model can check this. The closest proxy is Auntie Jo reading it aloud: it should sound like something she would say, fit inside the card, and contain only things that are true of Priya (turning 9 this Sunday, horses, Harry Potter).

deeper task:
Write a short birthday card message, 3-4 lines that fit by hand inside a card with a horse on the front, from Priya's Auntie Jo to Priya, who turns 9 this Sunday and is obsessed with horses and the Harry Potter books. Write in Auntie Jo's warm, playful voice, aimed at a 9-year-old. Use one clever touch that blends horses and Harry Potter (such as a Hogwarts-letter-style opening or a Hippogriff joke), mention turning 9, and end with a loving sign-off from "Auntie Jo." Don't invent specific memories, favorite characters, or horse names. Give just the card text, complete and ready to write, with no blanks or notes.

answers.plain:
Dear Priya,

Happy 9th Birthday! 🎉

I hope your day is full of magic, galloping fun, and maybe even a letter from Hogwarts. You're turning 9 and you're already braver than a Gryffindor and as graceful as a Hippogriff.

I hope this year brings you lots of adventures, great books, and many happy hours with horses.

Lots of love and a great big hug,
Auntie Jo 🐴✨
answers.nudge:
Here's my main pick, followed by two alternatives.

**Main pick (fits inside a card)**

> Dear Priya,
>
> Happy 9th Birthday! 🎉
>
> I hope your day is full of magic. Maybe a little Hogwarts-style magic, and a lot of galloping. Nine is a great age. Old enough to be brave like a Gryffindor, and young enough to still believe a horse might just be the best friend a witch could have.
>
> I hope this year brings you wonderful books, big adventures, and every wish you make on your candles.
>
> With all my love,
> Auntie Jo 🐴⚡

**Shorter version (if your card has less room)**

> Happy 9th Birthday, Priya!
>
> I hope your day is full of magic, cake, and maybe a pony or two. Keep reading, keep riding, and keep being brave.
>
> Love always,
> Auntie Jo

**Playful version (with a wink at Harry Potter)**

> Dear Priya,
>
> I solemnly swear that this is going to be your best birthday yet! 🪄
>
> Nine years old and already as brave as a hero and as wonderful as a unicorn. I hope your year is full of good stories and good rides.
>
> Lots of love,
> Auntie Jo

**Tips for writing it in the card**
- Pencil it in lightly first so you can check the spacing. The main pick takes about 6 to 7 lines on most cards.
- If you'd like to add a personal touch, a small lightning bolt or horseshoe doodle next to your name is a nice finish.
- If you know her favorite horse or her favorite Harry Potter book or character, swap it in. Something like "I hope you get to ride a Hippogriff-sized adventure" is the kind of detail she'll love.

I can also tailor it if you tell me something specific about Priya, such as whether she rides, her Hogwarts house, or a favorite in-joke.
